2.0.s.en: (1) Holding fast to the salvation of Christ offered to us

2.0.0.en: The things which we have heard: the teachings of Christianity.

2.0.1.en: Lest we should let them slip: we know them in theory and then neglect to apply them in our lives.

2.0.2.en: If Christ is greater than the angels, then we ought to give heed to the teachings of Christianity about the salvation offered on the Cross, which is greater and more perfect than the teachings of the Old Testament delivered by the hands of angels, so that we may apply them and live by them.

2.1.0.en: The word spoken by angels: the Law which Moses received from God by the hands of angels (Acts 7:53, Gal 3:19). If the word of God given to Moses through angels was strong and steadfast and could not be changed, because it was from God and whoever transgressed it was punished, as appeared in the history of the Jewish people when they neglected the Law and received severe punishments such as the captivity, how much more shall he be punished who neglects the salvation offered by Christ Himself, the Word of God, who became incarnate and redeemed us on the Cross and taught us His commandments Himself, and then the disciples and Apostles, who heard His teachings themselves and saw His crucifixion and resurrection, explained His teachings to us. This salvation is greater and more perfect than the salvation offered in the law of the Old Testament, because in the Old Testament the word of God was by the hands of angels, but in the New Testament Christ, the Word of God Himself, saves mankind by His redemption. And Christ confirmed this salvation when He strengthened His disciples and Apostles with miracles and the gifts of the Holy Spirit, such as preaching and speaking in tongues.

2.1.1.en: May you think of the love of Christ the Redeemer, crucified for your sake, and let it be the center of your daily life, so that you meditate on Him and thank Him, that your heart may be reassured of Christ's care for you, and respond to His love with many prayers, and with service and mercy toward those around you.

2.2.s.en: (2) The submission of believers to Christ

2.2.0.en: The world to come: the believers in the Church, and then in eternity.

2.2.1.en: The Jews believed that the archangel Michael was responsible for the care of the Jewish people, and that the other peoples were under the care of other angels. But in the New Testament the believers in the Church enjoy not only the care of the angels but also the salvation of Christ Himself, who is the Head of the Church, and then their submission to Him is completed in eternity, where the power of Satan is abolished and they belong to Christ with their whole being in continual praise.

2.3.0.en: One: the prophet David in (Ps 8:4). The prophet David speaks of weak, fallen humanity in need of salvation, expressing it by “man,” and how God cared for its salvation and visited it by sending His only Son Jesus Christ incarnate, who took the form of the Son of Man as a human being, setting aside His divine glory in order to redeem mankind. So, while in the form of man, He was lower than the angels, and this humility was for a short time, namely the period of His Incarnation, and after it He accomplished redemption and rose from the dead and ascended into the heavens, and appeared in the crown of glory and honor which was His from eternity, and gave salvation to those who believe in Him, who are the work of His hands and are subject to Him because He bought them with His blood.

2.3.1.en: These words apply not only to Christ but also to the spiritual man who believes in Him, for Christ gives him grace and awe in the eyes of others, so that they esteem him and feel his greatness because of his inner peace and the work of God with him, although he appears in many seasons to be in a state of weakness and enduring sufferings; then God's glory for him is completed when he receives the heavenly crown.

2.4.0.en: Thou hast put all things in subjection under his feet: this is the text of the psalm (Ps 8:6). Things: the Gentiles, for the believers from all the Gentiles have submitted to Him.

2.4.1.en: Christ died for the redemption of all mankind, Jews and Gentiles; all who believe in Him have submitted to Him, and not only the Jewish people. But the Apostle then adds that in the world there are still many who refuse to believe in Christ and do not submit to Him, because submission will be completed in eternity, when the believers are glorified in the Kingdom and the unbelievers are punished in eternal torment.

2.4.2.en: Give me, my Lord Jesus, the grace of submission to You, for in submission to You is all life. Grant that I may not share with the world in its sins, for which it rejects You, but let all my words and deeds be according to Your commandments, and let my thoughts also be pure before You, so that You may be glorified in me and I may be a light in Your hand to the world around me.

2.5.0.en: But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels: Jesus Christ in His Incarnation humbled Himself and appeared lower than the angels in honor.

2.5.1.en: Crowned with glory and honour: by His resurrection and ascension into the heavens. Christ was also crowned with the crown of love on the Cross and the crown of victory over Satan by His death, for by His death He trampled down death.

2.5.2.en: For the suffering of death: because He endured all the sufferings of the Cross and death, He rose crowned with glory and honor.

2.5.3.en: By the grace of God: the power of Christ's divinity, which sustained Him in enduring the sufferings and death.

2.5.4.en: That he should taste death: he did not say die but taste death, that is, He died for a short time, three days, so that those who believe in Him would not fear death, for it is the bridge of their crossing to the blessed eternity through Christ's redemption of them. For every man: Christ's death and redemption were for everyone who believes in Him, to receive salvation. So instead of man dying, Christ died for him, that he might live in Christ.

2.5.5.en: Christ humbled Himself by His Incarnation and became like us and endured suffering and death for us, and then His glory appeared by His resurrection and ascension, so that we would not fear death and would trust in the crowns that await us if we remain steadfast in faith in Him.

2.5.6.en: Your way to experience spiritual consolations and God's blessings in your life is through enduring the sufferings of life with thanksgiving for God's sake, and you can experience greater depths in fellowship with God when you endure sufferings in place of others, such as the labors of service, or bearing accusations over mistakes made by someone else, without defending yourself so as to cover for him. This is the way of redemption which Christ made for your sake, so you make it for the sake of others, and then Christ reveals Himself to you in a way you have not known before.

2.6.0.en: It became him: the Jews were waiting for a Messiah to save them from the Romans, and they stumbled when He suffered and was crucified and died; so Paul answers that the Father wants these sufferings to be accomplished in His Son for the salvation of mankind. This is what is fitting in the sight of God.

2.6.2.en: For whom are all things: the only purpose of creation is to praise and glorify God.

2.6.3.en: By whom are all things: all creation was created by the hand of God.

2.6.4.en: Many sons: those who believe in Christ.

2.6.5.en: Glory: the blessings of the New Testament in the Church, and then the glories of the Kingdom.

2.6.6.en: To make perfect ... through sufferings: Christ completes His saving work by enduring all the sufferings of the Cross and death in order to redeem mankind; this is the desire of the heart of the Father and the Son, that His children be saved from death.

2.6.7.en: The captain of their salvation: the Maker of salvation for all believers, that is, Christ.

2.6.8.en: It shows the participation of the Father and the Son in accomplishing redemption in that the Father, who is the Creator of all mankind and the goal of their life and who seeks their salvation, saw fit to give up His beloved Son for the redemption of His children who would believe in Him, completing every punishment of sin on their behalf and paying the debt before divine justice, so that He gives them complete salvation.

2.7.0.en: He that sanctifieth: Christ, who set Himself apart for the salvation of those who believe in Him.

2.7.1.en: They who are sanctified: those who believe in Christ, who have dedicated their lives to God and received their salvation.

2.7.2.en: One: God the Creator of all, or Adam the father of all mankind.

2.7.3.en: The humility of Christ in His Incarnation, which made Him for a little while lower than the angels, enabled Him to share the flesh with those who believe in Him, and He united with them in the origin, who is Adam, so He became a man like them, and likewise He united with them in sonship to God, but with a difference, since Christ is the Son of God by nature and essence, whereas men are sons by adoption. And since He shared humanity with men, He is not ashamed, despite His unlimited divine greatness, to call those who believe in Him brethren. By this He raised all believers to the sonship of God, though they are merely His creatures; but through the Incarnation they became brethren of Christ and sons of God.

2.7.4.en: It is wondrous humility on Your part, O God, to call me, the lowly one, Your brother; yet I rejoice, for this honor encourages me to draw near to You in prayer; and on the other hand it urges me to call all who are younger than I in age or lower in rank my brethren and to treat them with all love and humility, as You treat me.

2.8.0.en: The church: it is the Church of the New Testament, and in the original of the psalm “the congregation” was written, that is, the congregation of believers, which is the Church.

2.8.1.en: Paul confirms his words with a verse from the Old Testament (Ps 22:22), which speaks in the voice of Christ, who preached to mankind and gave them salvation and called them His brethren because of His sharing the flesh with them, and then they share with Him in praising God within the Church, which is His Body.

2.9.0.en: The Apostle quotes from (Isa 8:17) a prophecy about Christ, who by His Incarnation shared with mankind, so He speaks on their behalf to God in putting trust in Him, that we may receive by His grace obedience to God and trust in Him in everything.

2.9.1.en: He also quotes from (Isa 8:18) a prophecy about the incarnate Christ the Redeemer, who addresses those who believe in Him as a father, and presents them as His children before the Father to unite them with Himself so that they live with Him forever. And he said “again” twice in this verse because the first meaning is that Christ is a representative of mankind and the second is that He is a father to it.

2.9.2.en: The way to God has become easy through Christ, who gives us boldness and confidence in our relationship with Him, and teaches us how to obey Him and wait for Him however long our petition is delayed and our problems increase, so that we trust in Him, confident of His fatherhood and love, and press on Him in faith so as to experience Him more than before.

2.10.1.en: Flesh and blood: human nature; this confirms the humanity of Christ and refutes all the heresies that reject this.

2.10.4.en: A new benefit which mankind received by the Incarnation of Christ, which is the abolition of the authority of eternal death over those who believe in Him, for by His death He trampled down death, and the devil, the accuser of mankind, no longer has authority to take them after death to hell and eternal torment with him, because Christ by His Incarnation and redemption set them free and gave them life with Him in Paradise and the Kingdom.

2.11.1.en: The Incarnation of Christ proclaimed the union of God with man as a preparation for his redemption by the Cross, to set free His children, mankind, who were sentenced to death because of their sins. And in their fear of eternal death they became enslaved to the devil, and this drove them to fall into various sins. So the Incarnation of Christ frees them from the authority of the devil and the fear of death and every sin.

2.12.0.en: He took on him: does not rescue.

2.12.1.en: Angels: those who fell, that is, the demons.

2.12.2.en: The seed of Abraham: everyone who has the faith of Abraham, whether Jews or Gentiles.

2.12.3.en: The incarnate Christ the Redeemer did not come to save the demons, because they refuse repentance and persist in sin and tempt man and make him fall in open defiance of God, but He became incarnate to save the people who believe in Him, and since they have the faith of Abraham He calls them the seed of Abraham with respect to faith and not the flesh; He saves the Jews and the Gentiles, but he said Abraham because he is speaking to the Hebrews and Abraham is the father of faith acknowledged among them.

2.13.1.en: In all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren: Christ becomes a perfect man, body and soul, so that He is like the rest of mankind, and in humility He calls them His brethren.

2.13.2.en: Another reason for the Incarnation of Christ is that men may feel that He is like them in their human nature, so they feel His tenderness toward them and His nearness to them, and He gives them their needs and feels their sufferings. Then He comes forward as the High Priest of the New Testament, not to make atonement, like the high priest in the Old Testament, by sprinkling the blood of animals on the ark of God's covenant, but He offers His blood on the Cross to take away our sins, and in this He is faithful in accomplishing redemption and delivering His people from death and supporting them in all their afflictions.

2.14.0.en: Christ endured in His life on earth many sufferings, whether by direct temptations from Satan to make Him fall into pride and the lusts of the world, or by enduring insults, torments and persecutions up to the Cross, so that every person in temptation and affliction feels that Christ suffered the pains of temptations like him, and feels with him and sympathizes with him and supports him and comforts him during the temptation.

2.14.1.en: If God sympathizes with you in your afflictions, may you make those around you feel your sympathy with them. Merely listening to their complaints or encouraging them with kind words comforts their souls, how much more if you complete your love for them with works of mercy and help, so that they rejoice with you.

2.14.2.en: It is noticed from the foregoing that Christ gave us many blessings by His Incarnation, which are:

2.14.3.en: 1- Our being called brethren of Christ.

2.14.4.en: 2- Praising God in Christ and with His help.

2.14.5.en: 3- Trusting in God and obeying Him.

2.14.8.en: 6- Being strengthened in temptations because Christ is with us and feels with us.

3.0.0.en: Wherefore: based on what was mentioned before in the second chapter.

3.0.1.en: Brethren: Paul feels his fellowship with the Jews who became Christians in the Body of Christ.

3.0.2.en: Holy: the Christians, because they are dedicated to Christ.

3.0.3.en: The heavenly calling: the calling of Christ, which he describes as heavenly because He came down from heaven and will raise us to Him in heaven, in Paradise and the Kingdom, and also because His commandments are lofty and spiritual.

3.0.4.en: Consider: that is, contemplate and understand the saving work of Christ.

3.0.5.en: The Apostle of our profession: Christ, sent from the Father to us by His Incarnation so that we may see God before us and confess and believe in Him, and Christ declared, saying, “He that hath seen me hath seen the Father” (Jn 14:9). The sending of the Son does not mean His separation from the Father, but He is with Him at all times and fills every place despite His Incarnation.

3.0.6.en: High Priest: Christ is the High Priest of the New Testament, who offered the sacrifice of Himself on the Cross as an atonement for our sins, in place of the high priest in the Old Testament, who offered on one day in the year, the Day of Atonement, the blood of animals and sprinkled it on the ark of the covenant as a symbol of the blood of Christ the Redeemer. Because the Lord Christ is able to help those who are tempted, therefore, brethren in Christ Jesus, who made us all brethren in Him, you who have been called to enjoy heavenly joy, look closely and contemplate our Lord Jesus Christ, this One who came to connect us with heaven, who came to take our confession of the true faith and enter with it into the Holy of Holies of heaven itself, and not like the high priest in the Old Testament, who was in the Aaronic priesthood (Deut 26:3).

3.1.0.en: Appointed him: the Father sent the Son into the world to redeem it, and this does not mean the separation of the Son from the Father, because they are one in essence, and His being sent means the Incarnation and not His moving from one place to another, because despite His Incarnation He still fills every place with His divinity.

3.1.1.en: His house: His people, whom He shepherded and led in the wilderness for 40 years.

3.1.2.en: The Lord Jesus was faithful to God in the mission for which He came, just as Moses was faithful among the people of the children of Israel. It is noticed that St. Paul did not begin by preferring Christ to Moses, because Moses is the greatest of the prophets of the children of Israel, so he began by speaking of the likeness of Christ in faithfulness to Moses: Christ accomplished redemption on the Cross as Moses accomplished the shepherding of his people, and in the following verses he showed the superiority of Christ to Moses.

3.2.1.en: The house: the people of Israel, of whom Moses was one of the members.

3.2.2.en: This noble Person, that is, our Lord Jesus Christ, is worthy of much more glory than Moses by the same difference of glory between God the builder of the house and the house.

3.3.0.en: The house: the tabernacle of the congregation, that is, the temple of the Old Testament.

3.3.1.en: The greatness of Moses comes from his building of the tabernacle of the congregation, but Christ is the Creator of all mankind, among them Moses, and He is responsible for the redemption of all mankind and not only the people of Israel. Moses is a faithful servant of God, but Christ is God Himself, the Creator of all and the Redeemer of all.

3.4.0.en: As a servant, for a testimony: he completes his service, which prepares for and bears witness to Christ who comes after him.

3.4.1.en: Those things which were to be spoken after: the teachings of Christ.

3.4.2.en: As a son over his own house: the Master and Owner of everything, because He is the Creator and the Redeemer, and He is the Head of the Church and its Savior.

3.4.3.en: The faithfulness of Moses was a faithfulness entrusted to him as a servant in the tabernacle of the congregation and for the shepherding of the children of Israel, but the faithfulness of the Lord Christ over the souls of mankind, which is us, is the faithfulness of the Owner of everything, because He is God the Creator and Redeemer. And we Christians will enjoy the blessings of His faithfulness and His great redeeming work for our sake if we remain steadfast in confidence in His person and hold fast the hope which the Lord Jesus gives us.

3.4.4.en: So when St. Paul compared the difference of glory between our Lord Jesus Christ and the prophet Moses, we can say that he compared in two basic respects:

3.4.5.en: A - The breadth of the faithfulness of the person of our Lord Jesus Christ (the Builder of all) compared with Moses and his faithfulness over the house of Israel.

3.4.6.en: B - The authority of the Lord Jesus as a Son in His house (the whole) and the work of Moses as a servant in the house of Israel.

3.4.7.en: May you hold fast to your hope in God however troubles surround you or the devil's wars increase against you or your falls multiply, for Christ is able to raise you up from all these; and if you suffer and endure, lift your eyes to the hope of eternity, in which your Christ will compensate you with inexpressible joys and glories.

3.5.0.en: Wherefore: because you are children of God who believe in Him, as the preceding verse indicates.

3.5.1.en: The Holy Ghost: through the mouth of David in (Ps 95:7-11). To day: he means the literal meaning, that is, today for the hearer when God speaks to him in the Holy Bible or alerts him by any means, so that he does not neglect it or disobey.

3.5.2.en: Harden: the heart means the center of the emotions, so that man should not make his heart stiff, devoid of feelings toward the word of God, and reject it.

3.5.3.en: The provocation: murmuring and intense anger.

3.5.4.en: The day of temptation: the day on which the children of Israel murmured against Moses because there was no water, and he struck the rock before them and it brought forth water, and the place was named Meribah or Massah (Ex 17:1-7). And Psalm (95) mentions the name Meribah to clarify the meaning of the day of temptation. What is meant here is not only the murmuring of the children of Israel at Meribah but their repeated murmuring in the wilderness of Sinai and before crossing into it.

3.5.5.en: The wilderness: the wilderness of Sinai.

3.5.6.en: St. Paul moves from the relation of Christ to Moses to His relation to His people, the Jews who became Christians, and calls them to obey Him and believe His teachings and not to doubt and murmur because of the ideas of the unbelieving Jews, and not to imitate their forefathers when they murmured against God before they crossed the Red Sea and during their wandering in the wilderness of Sinai when they were thirsty or found bitter water or grew weary of the manna ... etc. (Ex 14:11, Ex 16:3).

3.6.1.en: Proved me: they saw My care and concern for them and My ability to do miracles for them.

3.6.2.en: The children of Israel believed in God, the God of their fathers, but in the wilderness of Sinai they came to know God through His care and His provision for their needs and His leading of them, and that for a long time, forty years, but unfortunately throughout this period they tested God and angered Him and murmured many times, and He was patient and poured out His blessings upon them.

3.7.0.en: Wherefore: because of their testing of Me and their murmuring and their doubting My power.

3.7.2.en: This generation: the people of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai, and what is meant is their sins and not their persons, since He continued to shepherd them in the hope that they would repent.

3.7.3.en: They do alway err in their heart: they doubt and murmur, so their hearts turn away from Me and they think of material things. They have not known my ways: they did not believe and walk in a spiritual way of obedience and trust.

3.7.4.en: God was angry because of the people's murmuring against Him and their preoccupation with material things away from Him, so they did not live with Him, although the purpose of setting them apart as His people and bringing them out of Egypt was to devote themselves to the worship of God and to enjoy fellowship with Him, far from the disturbance of the idol worship in Egypt.

3.8.0.en: I sware: the prophet David in the psalm likens God to man in the oath, that is, the word which one does not go back on, in order to clarify the necessity of the fulfillment of God's word.

3.8.2.en: Because of the children of Israel's persistence in murmuring and unbelief, God decided to deprive them of entering the Promised Land, so He made them wander in the wilderness of Sinai forty years until all the adults who were attached to the land of Egypt died, and the children who were raised in the wilderness remained, and learned the worship of God and endured the hardships of the wilderness and saw God's care and believed in Him, so they deserved to enjoy His good things in the Promised Land. And none of the adults entered with them except two, who were distinguished by faith, namely Joshua and Caleb.

3.8.3.en: God calls you by different means, whether by His good things and gifts so that you thank Him, or by afflictions so that you take refuge in Him, or by His commandments, written or heard, so that you take heed and live with Him. So do not neglect His voice, but let today be an opportunity for you for repentance and renewing your covenants with Him, and He will pour out on you blessings you cannot imagine and you will delight in experiencing fellowship with Him.

3.9.0.en: St. Paul moves from his talk about the hardness of the hearts of the children of Israel and their murmuring in the wilderness to his purpose, which is to confirm the faith of the Jews who became Christians, so he warns them lest any man keep evil in his heart by doubting the Christian faith or accepting the words of the Jews who make them feel their deprivation of Jewish worship as though they had lost their relationship with God, so that none may return to Judaism because of these doubts but remain steadfast in his faith in Christ.

3.10.0.en: Exhort one another: admonish one another.

3.10.1.en: Daily: seizing every opportunity to confirm one another's faith.

3.10.2.en: While it is called To day: as long as there is an opportunity for repentance and life with God. The deceitfulness of sin: the lusts of sin and the pride that may result from them.

3.10.3.en: The Apostle Paul warns the believers to encourage one another so that they remain steadfast in faith in Christ, seizing every opportunity for teaching and preaching so that they do not lose their spiritual feelings toward God and fall into evil lusts and the pride into which the Jews fell because of their pride in being the chosen people and better than all mankind, so that they rejected Christ and faith in Him.

3.11.0.en: Partakers of Christ: our sharing in the faith and its blessings by our membership in the Church.

3.11.1.en: The beginning of our confidence: the faith with which we began.

3.11.2.en: He clarifies the greatness of the blessings which the believers enjoy in the Church, since they have become members in the Body of Christ and receive the Holy Sacraments and enjoy the means of grace such as prayers and fasts. All this if they remain until the end of their lives in the upright faith with which they began and do not listen to the doubts of the Jews.

3.12.0.en: He also reminds them to continue in their spiritual life and their living feelings toward God, so that they do not fall into murmuring and anger against God because of material lusts.

3.13.0.en: Provoked: angered God or made Him angry with them.

3.13.1.en: Although God brought the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by great miracles, the ten plagues, and divided the Red Sea before them, yet they went back and angered Him because of their murmuring and their disobedience in entering the Promised Land.

3.14.0.en: God hated the murmurings of the children of Israel and their unbelief and disobedience to Him in entering the Promised Land, so He made them wander in the wilderness forty years, in which all the adults died and their bodies were buried in the wilderness of Sinai, and they did not enter the Promised Land except Joshua and Caleb.

3.15.0.en: Believed not: they did not obey the word of God, that is, they did not believe it so as to obey it.

3.15.1.en: Because of the unbelief of the children of Israel and their murmuring, God decided to deprive them of entering the Promised Land.

3.16.0.en: St. Paul summarizes and states that unbelief is the reason for the deprivation of the children of Israel from enjoying God's promises in entering the Promised Land, which means their enjoying fellowship with Him and is a type of the heavenly Canaan.

3.16.1.en: Your continual relationship with God in the prayers and readings of every day confirms your faith in Him, so it is easy for you to obey His commandments. So seize every opportunity to be with God in the church and in your closet, and you will enjoy fellowship with Him on earth and in heaven.

3.16.2.en: A comparison between the rest in the land of Canaan and the rest in Christ. In this chapter a comparison between the rest on the Sabbath day and Joshua, who brought the people of God into rest in the Promised Land, and Christ, who brings those who believe in Him into the true rest in the Kingdom of Heaven.
